name: MPS Ltd
title: MPS Ltd - 532440 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: MPS FY26 revenue rose 5.7% to INR 768 crore and EBITDA 11.8% to INR 236 crore; FY27 EBITDA guided to comfortably exceed INR 300 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 was described as the most profitable year in company history, with EBITDA margin at 30.7% and PAT up 16.3% to INR 173 crore. Q4 revenue grew 12.7% to INR 205 crore and EBITDA margin expanded to 32.9%, helped by Research and the Unbound Medicine acquisition, which closed on 9 February 2026. Corporate Learning revenue fell 16.5% for the year but returned to positive year-on-year growth in Q4. Management guided FY27 EBITDA above INR 300 crore on an organic, bottom-up basis, and no final dividend was recommended for FY26 because capital was deployed into Unbound and the M&A pipeline.

financial_highlights.value: INR 113.75 crore; borrowings INR 40.25 crore (Unbound facility)

segments.name: Research Solutions
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 464 crore, EBITDA margin 39.9% (+330 bps); organic growth 17% ex-AJE. Q4 revenue INR 120 crore (+7.6% YoY), EBITDA INR 50 crore at 41.6% margin; organic core grew 23% YoY in Q4.

segments.name: Education Solutions
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 209 crore, organic growth 28.6%; EBITDA INR 82 crore at 39.2% margin, up 42.6% reported. Q4 revenue INR 60 crore (+30.5% YoY). Unbound contributed INR 11.78 crore over 50 days, about 19.6% of Q4 Education revenue.

segments.name: Corporate Learning (Liberate Global)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 96 crore, down 16.5% YoY; headcount down about 32% YoY. Q4 revenue INR 25.5 crore (+2.4% YoY, first positive print of year); Q4 EBITDA INR 6.7 crore at 26.3% margin, up 55% QoQ.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA to comfortably cross INR 300 crore, built bottom-up from segment plans; implies about 21% EBITDA CAGR FY24-FY27 and excludes any acquisitions beyond Unbound.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected in the 30%-35% range, with margins typically expanding as revenue grows.
Indicative FY27 split of EBITDA: Research about 55%, Education about 35%, Corporate Learning about 10% (management said it was ballpark only).

Unbound Medicine: FY27 monthly revenue expected at USD 750,000-950,000 (seasonal), starting at about 15% EBITDA margin and exiting at 25%-30%; historical run rate USD 700,000-800,000 per month at 18%-19% margin.
FY28 target of about INR 1,500 crore revenue (Vision 2027) reaffirmed as intact; tighter FY28 guidance to be given at end of Q3 or Q4 FY27.
No final dividend for FY26; management said distributions resume when the current deployment cycle closes.
capex_capacity: Unbound Medicine acquisition closed 9 February 2026; first 50 days contributed INR 11.78 crore revenue; integration into full operating year in FY27.

Acquisition pipeline of 35 companies: 5 fairly advanced, 5 live, 2 at advanced stage; most advanced is a Higher Ed and Online Learning carve-out in the Western world. Management said pricing discipline and the Unbound return threshold apply.
MPS Labs is a 200-engineer AI R&D team; Think365 platform in live production after about 2 years of build.
Research Integrity Check (RIC) and DigiCore Pro scaling across renewal cohort; JEO office (pre-acceptance) identified as the highest-margin Research line.
Corporate Learning shifting to AI, AR/VR and simulation-led builds; Bridge AI multilingual translation in active enterprise deployment.
demand_pricing: Research: pre-acceptance (B2B) services grew more than 90%; AJE pruning described as complete. AJE growth drivers are premium author tiers, AI-driven productivity, and cross-selling to corporate publishers.
Early China and APAC expansion: a few MOUs signed and operations initiated with Chinese publishers; Japan also flagged as a target.
Education: AI-accessibility line (more than 30 million auto-generated accessible media assets a year) roughly tripled revenue in FY26.
Corporate Learning: Q4 order book the strongest of FY26; new entrants added at top customer relationships.
Management argued AI commoditises basic production work and raises demand for trusted, verified AI in high-stakes knowledge workflows; company's share of serviceable market is about 0.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is MPS's right to win in a market where it holds only about 0.5% share, and what capabilities are needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited an AI-first knowledge positioning in high-stakes layers, an integrated platform stack (HighWire, Think365, RIC, Bridge AI, Unbound, DigiCore), 200+ MPS Labs engineers, and deep expansion within large accounts. The target path is 0.5% to 1% to 2% over several years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 1,500 crore FY28 revenue target still achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is intact and in line of sight. FY27 INR 300 crore EBITDA is organic and excludes new acquisitions; any further M&A would sit on top. Tighter FY28 guidance to come at end-Q3 or Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Are there more acquisitions, and has Unbound been paid for?
qa_highlights.answer: Unbound is mostly fully paid, with only small closing amounts left. Pipeline is active, with a Western Higher Ed carve-out the most advanced. Management will disclose material deals in the ordinary course.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA margin expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a margin in the 30%-35% range, with expansion as revenue grows.

qa_highlights.question: What is Unbound's revenue and EBITDA, and how will it move in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The 50-day consolidation gave INR 11-12 crore revenue at 18.5%-19% margin. Monthly run rate was USD 700,000-800,000. FY27 expected USD 750,000-950,000 per month, starting near 15% EBITDA margin and exiting at 25%-30%.

qa_highlights.question: Given AI disruption, what protects the business model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI compresses commoditised production work but raises demand for trusted AI in medicine, scholarly publishing and regulated learning. It sees agentic AI as a tailwind, with verification as the gating constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margin dip and ex-AJE headcount rise, and what drives FY27 growth and the FY28 path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AJE headcount moved offshore to India while Research headcount rose ahead of expected growth, causing a timing-related ex-AJE margin softness in Q4. Growth drivers are the four Research product layers, Education, and the accessibility line.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Corporate Learning investment shift, and why did clients rise while revenue per client fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Work has moved from compliance content to AI, AR/VR and simulation-led performance enablers. Unbound added a long tail of smaller institutional accounts, which lowered average revenue per client without any anchor client billing less.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA split and main risk to the INR 300 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave a ballpark split of Research 55%, Education 35%, Corporate 10%. It sees no company-specific risk, only broader geopolitical and macro risk. Management disputed the analyst's constant-currency framing.

risks_watch: AI-driven price compression in commoditised AJE and copy-editing work; management says the book has been pruned and high-value core remains.
Ex-AJE Research margin softness in Q4 from headcount added ahead of growth; watch whether margins hold in FY27.
Corporate Learning must sustain the Q4 exit margin of 26.3%; FY26 revenue fell 16.5%.
Unbound integration: margin to slip from about 18.5%-19% toward 15% in early FY27 before the 25%-30% exit target; lower revenue per client as the long tail of accounts is added.
Dividend suspended for FY26; capital deployment for M&A ahead of cash on hand.
FY28 INR 1,500 crore revenue target requires a step-up from about 6% run-rate growth noted by an analyst; tighter guidance due end-FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-leaning on FY27 EBITDA and the long-term target, with the CEO calling the guidance conservative. Evasive on Unbound exact financials (ranges only), acquisition targets and margin split, and dismissive of the constant-currency question. Cautious on the AJE tailing effect and Corporate Learning, which management described as a reset year.
key_quotes: The guidance also reflects that we are already in flight, and this is not a step change we are asking you to believe.
The INR 300-plus crores EBITDA mark is not a stretch target. It is a number we have built our operating plan around.
Capital earns its keep within 12 months or gets returned to shareholders.
The bottleneck in research today is no longer generation; it is verification.

growth.why: FY27 EBITDA guided to comfortably cross INR 300 crore (vs FY26 INR 236 crore, roughly 27% growth), with a 30-35% margin and Unbound at USD 750k-950k monthly, backed by segment plans and Unbound run rate but with no specific new capacity, order or contract numbers given beyond the acquisition.
